newsitem.title: TAIWAN: AT&T, Taiwan Chunghwa to sign Internet deal.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Taiwan Chunghwa to sign Internet deal.

text.p: U.S. giant AT&T Corp said on Monday it would sign a deal with Chunghwa Telecommunication Corp on Wednesday to provide the Taiwan state-run telecom firm with high-speed digital data lines for the Internet.
AT&T, in a statement, said the deal would allow Chunghwa to improve and increase its Internet service in order to meet an ongoing explosion in Taiwan's cyberspace market.
AT&T and Chunghwa declined to reveal further details.
"All the details, like the signing amount and term and number of lines, will be revealed at the signing ceremony on Wednesday," an AT&T spokeswoman said by telephone.
Chunghwa is competing with several domestic companies, including computer giant First International Computer, to provide Internet service in Taiwan's fully liberalised value-added telecom market.
The semi-official Institute for Information Industry estimates the number of Internet users in Taiwan at 400,000, but says the total is bounding higher by the day.

AT&T, in a consortium led by Taiwan's Far Eastern group, became one of several foreign companies to gain access to Taiwan's once-closed telecommunication market when it won one of eight mobile phone operation licences awarded in March.

Taiwan still caps foreign ownership of telephony and other basic common carrier services at 20 percent, though this is expected to rise to 30 percent as Taiwan pushes to enter the World Trade Organisation.
There are no restrictions on foreign ownership of value-added services such as Internet.
